messages:
alex: Customer cust_993 (trial) reports that their credits did not decrease after three batch embeddings calls. They attached their curl and got 200 + embeddings each time but UI balance stayed the same.

maria (billing): Can you paste the request IDs and timestamps? we'll look up ledger events.

alex: Sure. Calls were at 2025-03-05T14:17:12Z / req=01a7f, 14:22:39Z / req=02b1c, 14:28:01Z / req=03c9d. Sample request: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX' \n  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 20250305-req01' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":["hi","ok","a"]}'``` Response: 200, payload with three embedding vectors.

support-bot: Received webhook: proxy forwarded x-request-id=proxy-9f3, upstream-status=200, upstream-request-id=req-01a7f.

maria (billing): I searched ledger for cust_993 around those times — no usage events tied to those request IDs. UI shows trial balance unchanged.

sre-josh: I pulled the proxy and runtime logs. Upstream closed with 200 and we returned embeddings. I also grabbed the token-estimator output for those requests: estimator returned 0 tokens for each input (they were single chars). Example from runtime logs: `token_estimate: 0, model: rwd-embed-1, inputs: ["hi","ok","a"]`

alex: Wait — estimator reported 0? But embeddings were generated, so tokens must have been consumed.

eng-runtime: Quick summary from runtime triage: we rolled a micro-optimizing tokenizer change last week that computes token lengths using a fast byte-length heuristic and short-circuits to 0 for inputs under 3 bytes to speed up batching. That heuristic wasn't mirrored in the billing path and the billing ingestion pipeline expects a token count > 0 to emit a usage event. For small inputs the estimator produced 0 -> ingestion dropped the usage event -> no ledger entry.

maria (billing): Ugh. So server did the work and we didn't record it. Impact: customers making micro-embedding batches (many tiny strings) might not see consumption reflected.

sre-josh: Root cause identified. Repro steps:
1) Send embeddings with inputs all <3 bytes (e.g., "a", "ok")
2) Observe runtime logs showing `token_estimate: 0`
3) Check billing ingestion topic -> no usage messages emitted.

eng-runtime: I've prepared a hotfix PR that removes the short-circuit and uses the tokenizer's canonical token count for billing attribution. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/1428. Rolling to canary now.

maria (billing): Mitigation plan for affected customers: 1) Run backfill to scan proxy logs for request IDs with upstream-status=200 and no ledger event; 2) Generate synthetic usage events based on actual token counts from runtime logs; 3) Credit customers where we can't reconstruct token counts.

alex: Can we do a targeted credit for cust_993 first? They were pretty upset.

maria (billing): Yes. I'll queue a manual override. Based on runtime vectors size, estimate ~0.002 credits per short embed x 3 calls x 10 items = 0.06 credits. I'll round to 0.1 credit and apply now.

support-bot: Action logged: billing_override created by maria for cust_993 amount=0.1 credits (ref: OVERRIDE-20250305-7).

sre-josh: Canary patch is in prod-canary. I also scheduled the ingestion backfill job to lock on the proxy topic from 2025-03-05T14:00:00Z to 2025-03-05T15:00:00Z. ETA for backfill completion: ~45m.

maria (billing): Backfill finished. We created usage events for ~12 customers; cust_993 got 0.12 credits applied + the manual 0.1 override (total 0.22). I notified them with a support note.

alex: Customer confirmed — balance updated and they acknowledged. Thanks.

eng-runtime: Postmortem notes: revert heuristic, add e2e test for tiny-input embeddings, add alerts for mismatch between upstream-status=200 and lack of usage events for same request ids.

maria (billing): I'll prepare a short status email and mark as resolved after 24h. cc @eng-runtime @sre. :white_check_mark:
